items.followUp: State the two conditions for equilibrium and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Checks the condition for translational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant force is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net or resultant force is zero.

rubric.why: Checks that the translational condition is illustrated by an example.
rubric.description: Gives an example of translational equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example in which forces balance.

rubric.why: Checks the condition for rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant torque or moment is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net or resultant torque or moment is zero.

rubric.why: Checks that the rotational condition is illustrated by an example.
rubric.description: Gives an example of rotational equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example showing balanced moments or no turning effect.

modelAnswer: Translational equilibrium: the resultant force acting on a body is zero, ΣF = 0.
Example: a book resting on a table has its weight balanced by the table’s upward force.
Rotational equilibrium: the resultant torque (moment) about any point is zero, Στ = 0.
Example: a balanced seesaw has equal clockwise and anticlockwise moments.

items.followUp: A car weighs 8,000 N and moves at 15 m/s. Find its kinetic energy. Take g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: Checks conversion of the given weight to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly converting 12 kN to 12,000 N.

rubric.why: Checks the calculation of mass from weight.
rubric.description: Finds the car’s mass using m = W/g.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining 1,200 kg using g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: Checks selection of the kinetic-energy formula.
Checks substitution of the mass and speed into the formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given values with units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution using 1,200 kg and 20 m/s.

rubric.why: Checks the evaluated result and its unit.
rubric.description: States the kinetic energy with an appropriate unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 240,000 J or an equivalent energy value with a correct unit.

modelAnswer: Given: W = 12 kN = 12,000 N, v = 20 m/s, g = 10 m/s².

items.followUp: A hydraulic press has a large piston of diameter 40 cm and a small piston of diameter 4 cm. What force must be applied to the small piston to lift a load of 12,000 N?

rubric.why: Checks conversion of the piston diameters to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for converting 30 cm to 0.30 m and 3 cm to 0.03 m.

rubric.why: Checks use of Pascal’s principle for the hydraulic press.
rubric.description: Equates the pressure at the two pistons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using equal pressure or the equivalent force-to-area relation.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship between piston area and diameter.
rubric.description: Uses the squared diameter ratio to relate the piston areas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly using the small-to-large diameter ratio squared.

rubric.why: Checks substitution and calculation of the applied force.
rubric.description: Substitutes the load and diameter ratio and calculates the small-piston force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or calculation.

rubric.why: Checks the final force and its unit.
rubric.description: States the force required to lift the car.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 200 N or an equivalent force with a correct unit.

modelAnswer: Given: large-piston diameter = 30 cm = 0.30 m; small-piston diameter = 3 cm = 0.03 m; load on large piston = 20,000 N.
Since A = πd²/4, Asmall/Alarge = (0.03 m/0.30 m)² = (0.03/0.30)².

items.followUp: What is the least count of a measuring instrument? State how the least count of vernier callipers is found.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of least count.
rubric.description: Defines least count as the smallest length measurable accurately by the instrument.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the smallest accurately measurable length or value.

rubric.why: Checks the least-count relation for vernier callipers.
rubric.description: States that least count is one main-scale division minus one vernier-scale division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct difference relation.

modelAnswer: The least count of vernier callipers is the smallest length that can be measured accurately with them.
Least count = value of 1 main-scale division − value of 1 vernier-scale division.

items.followUp: What is zero error in vernier callipers, and how is it related to zero correction?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of zero correction.
rubric.description: Defines zero correction as the correction applied to a measurement to remove zero error.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the correction applied to a measurement with removal of zero error.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship between zero correction and zero error.
rubric.description: States that zero correction has equal magnitude and opposite sign to zero error.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct magnitude-and-sign relationship or its equation.

modelAnswer: Zero correction is the correction applied to an observed measurement to remove zero error.
It is equal in magnitude and opposite in sign to the zero error: zero correction = − zero error.
